newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: U.S. Secret Service awards Cambodian ministers.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Secret Service awards Cambodian ministers.

text.p: The U.S. Secret Service presented awards on Friday to Cambodia's co-Interior Ministers for helping crack a major counterfeiting operation.
Secret Service special agent James Davison presented awards to police and interior officials, including ministers Sar Kheng and You Hockry, at a ceremony in the U.S. Ambassador's residence.

The Cambodians were honoured for catching Japanese Red Army fugitive Hoshimi Tanaka, wanted in Thailand for running a multi-million dollar counterfeiting ring in Thailand and at home for hijacking a plane.
Tanaka was arrested in March last year while trying to drive across the border into Vietnam with three North Korean diplomats based at Pyongyang's embassy in Phnom Penh.
The Japanese, now on trial in Thailand for counterfeiting, was also wanted at home for his suspected role in hijacking an aircraft to North Korea in 1970.

Ambassador Kenneth Quinn said Tanaka was "the most important person in the biggest case the U.S. Secret Service has ever pursued" and added that the Cambodian government responded "magnificently" to request for help.
Davison said investigations were continuing into the case.
U.S. Secret Service Assistant Director Paul Hackenbury, in charge of all criminal investigations worldwide for the service, attended the ceremony.
